name: England
fact: England and Scotland played the first official international match in 1872, a 0–0 draw in Glasgow. England's only World Cup win came at home in 1966.

name: Scotland
fact: Scotland played in the world's first official international, against England in 1872. Celtic became the first British club to win the European Cup, in 1967.

name: Wales
fact: Wales reached the semi-finals of Euro 2016, their first major tournament since the 1958 World Cup.

name: Northern Ireland
fact: Northern Ireland reached the World Cup quarter-finals at their first attempt in 1958. George Best, one of the greatest wingers ever, was born in Belfast.

name: Republic of Ireland
fact: The Republic of Ireland reached the quarter-finals of their first World Cup, in 1990.

name: Spain
fact: Spain won Euro 2008, the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 in a row, then won a record fourth European Championship in 2024.

name: France
fact: France have won the World Cup twice, in 1998 and 2018, and reached the final again in 2022.

name: Germany
fact: Germany have won four World Cups: three as West Germany (1954, 1974, 1990) and one as a unified Germany (2014).

name: Italy
fact: Italy have won four World Cups (1934, 1938, 1982 and 2006) and won Euro 2020, which was played in 2021.

name: Portugal
fact: Portugal won Euro 2016 and the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

name: Netherlands
fact: The Netherlands have reached three World Cup finals (1974, 1978 and 2010) without winning one. Their 1970s 'Total Football' changed how the game is played.

name: Belgium
fact: Belgium finished third at the 2018 World Cup, their best result ever.

name: Croatia
fact: Croatia, a country of under four million people, reached the 2018 World Cup final and finished third in both 1998 and 2022.

name: Denmark
fact: Denmark won Euro 1992 after being called up at short notice to replace Yugoslavia.

name: Norway
fact: Norway beat Brazil 2–1 at the 1998 World Cup, one of the great group-stage upsets.

name: Sweden
fact: Sweden hosted the 1958 World Cup and reached the final, losing 5–2 to Brazil.

name: Poland
fact: Poland have finished third at the World Cup twice, in 1974 and 1982.

name: Switzerland
fact: Switzerland hosted the 1954 World Cup. Both FIFA (in Zurich) and UEFA (in Nyon) have their headquarters there.

name: Austria
fact: Austria's 'Wunderteam' was one of Europe's best sides in the early 1930s, and Austria finished third at the 1954 World Cup.

name: Serbia
fact: Belgrade's Red Star won the European Cup in 1991, when the city was part of Yugoslavia.

name: Ukraine
fact: Ukraine reached the quarter-finals of their first World Cup, in 2006.

name: Türkiye
fact: Türkiye finished third at the 2002 World Cup, where Hakan Şükür scored the fastest goal in World Cup history, after 11 seconds.

name: Czechia
fact: Czechoslovakia reached the World Cup final in 1934 and 1962, and the Czech Republic reached the final of Euro 96.

name: Hungary
fact: Hungary's 'Mighty Magyars' beat England 6–3 at Wembley in 1953 and reached the 1954 World Cup final.

name: Georgia
fact: Georgia reached their first major tournament at Euro 2024 and made it to the round of 16.

name: Slovenia
fact: Slovenia, home to about two million people, has played at two World Cups, in 2002 and 2010.

name: Greece
fact: Greece were huge outsiders when they won Euro 2004, beating the hosts Portugal in the final.

name: Iceland
fact: Iceland, with fewer than 400,000 people, knocked England out of Euro 2016 and played at the 2018 World Cup.

name: Russia
fact: Russia hosted the 2018 World Cup. As the Soviet Union, the team won the first European Championship, in 1960.

name: Monaco
fact: AS Monaco is based in the tiny principality of Monaco but plays in the French league.

name: Brazil
fact: Brazil have won a record five World Cups (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002) and are the only team to have played at every World Cup.

name: Argentina
fact: Argentina have won three World Cups (1978, 1986 and 2022) and a record 16 Copa América titles.

name: Uruguay
fact: Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup in 1930, and won it again in Brazil in 1950.

name: Colombia
fact: Colombia's James Rodríguez won the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup with six goals.

name: Chile
fact: Chile won their first Copa América as hosts in 2015, then won it again in 2016.

name: Ecuador
fact: Ecuador's capital, Quito, sits about 2,850 metres above sea level, which makes home games tough for visiting teams.

name: Peru
fact: Peru have won the Copa América twice, in 1939 and 1975.

name: Mexico
fact: Mexico is the first country to host the men's World Cup three times: 1970, 1986 and 2026.

name: United States
fact: The USA reached the semi-finals of the first World Cup in 1930, hosted the 1994 tournament and co-hosted 2026 with Canada and Mexico.

name: Canada
fact: Canada played their first men's World Cup in 1986 and co-hosted the 2026 tournament.

name: Egypt
fact: Egypt have won the Africa Cup of Nations a record seven times.

name: Senegal
fact: Senegal beat the holders France in their first World Cup match in 2002 and went on to reach the quarter-finals.

name: Nigeria
fact: Nigeria won the Olympic gold medal in men's football at Atlanta 1996.

name: Morocco
fact: Morocco became the first African team to reach a World Cup semi-final, in 2022.

name: Ghana
fact: Ghana reached the 2010 World Cup quarter-finals and lost to Uruguay on penalties after Luis Suárez handled on the goal line.

name: Cameroon
fact: Cameroon were the first African team to reach a World Cup quarter-final, in 1990, when Roger Milla scored four goals at the age of 38.

name: Côte d'Ivoire
fact: Côte d'Ivoire won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2015, and again as hosts in the 2023 edition.

name: Algeria
fact: Algeria beat West Germany 2–1 at their first World Cup, in 1982.

name: Liberia
fact: Liberia's George Weah won the Ballon d'Or in 1995 and later became the country's president.

name: Japan
fact: Japan co-hosted the 2002 World Cup with South Korea, the first World Cup held in Asia.

name: South Korea
fact: South Korea reached the semi-finals of the 2002 World Cup, which they co-hosted. No other Asian team has gone that far.

name: Australia
fact: Australia moved from the Oceania confederation to Asia's in 2006 and won the Asian Cup in 2015.

name: Saudi Arabia
fact: Saudi Arabia beat the eventual champions Argentina 2–1 at the 2022 World Cup, and will host the 2034 tournament.

name: Qatar
fact: Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup, the first held in the Middle East and the first played in November and December.

name: United Arab Emirates
fact: The United Arab Emirates have played at one World Cup, in Italy in 1990.
